```{r}
# --- Step 5. Function: Facet by Genotype, Save All
plot_corr_iN_vs_iDA_by_genotype <- function(corr_mat, annot_class_df, annot_colors, gene_count_df, out_dir) {
  # Ensure matrix is a data frame
  corr_mat <- as.data.frame(corr_mat)

  # Get all genotypes (must have both iN and iDA)
  geno_base <- unique(gsub("_(iN|iDA)$", "", rownames(corr_mat)))
  valid_genos <- geno_base[
    paste0(geno_base, "_iN") %in% rownames(corr_mat) &
    paste0(geno_base, "_iDA") %in% rownames(corr_mat)
  ]

  # ---------- COLLECT ALL FOR FACET ----------
  all_df <- map_dfr(valid_genos, function(g) {
    iN_vec  <- corr_mat[paste0(g, "_iN"), ]
    iDA_vec <- corr_mat[paste0(g, "_iDA"), ]

    tibble(
      Genotype = g,
      Annotation = names(iN_vec),
      Cor_iN = as.numeric(iN_vec),
      Cor_iDA = as.numeric(iDA_vec)
    )
  }) %>%
    left_join(annot_class_df, by = "Annotation") %>%
    left_join(gene_count_df, by = "Annotation") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Class = factor(Class, levels = names(annot_colors)))

  # ---------- FACET-WRAPPED PLOT ----------
   p_facet <- ggplot(all_df, aes(x = Cor_iN, y = Cor_iDA, color = Class)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = GeneCount), alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_size(range = c(1, 8), breaks = c(10, 50, 100, 250, 500, 750, 1000), name = "Gene Count") +
    #scale_size_continuous(trans = "log10", range = c(1.5, 5), name = "Gene Count") +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = annot_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ Genotype, scales = "fixed") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 6) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) +
    labs(x = "iN Correlation", y = "iDA Correlation", title = "Annotation Correlation: iN vs iDA by Genotype")

  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "facet_bubbleplot_iN_vs_iDA_all.pdf"), p_facet, width = 15, height = 15, device = cairo_pdf)

  # ---------- INDIVIDUAL PLOTS ----------
  for (g in valid_genos) {
    df_g <- filter(all_df, Genotype == g)
    
    # write sourcedata for bubbleplots
    readr::write_csv(df_g, file.path(out_dir, paste0("iN_vs_iDA_bubble_", g, "_sourcedata.csv")))
    
    # Label only annotations from specific classes
    df_label_select <- df_g %>% filter(Class %in% c("Synaptic", "Endo", "Lyso"))
    axis_lim <- range(c(all_df$Cor_iN, all_df$Cor_iDA), na.rm = TRUE)
    
    p <- ggplot(df_g, aes(x = Cor_iN, y = Cor_iDA, color = Class)) +
      geom_point(aes(size = GeneCount), alpha = 0.8) +
      scale_size(range = c(1, 8), breaks = c(10, 50, 100, 250, 500, 750, 1000), name = "Gene Count") +
      #scale_size_continuous(trans = "log2", range = c(1, 8), name = "Gene Count") +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
      scale_color_manual(values = annot_colors, drop = FALSE) +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = axis_lim, ylim = axis_lim) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 6) +
      theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) +
      labs(
        title = paste("iN vs iDA Correlation —", g),
        x = "iN Correlation", y = "iDA Correlation"
      ) +
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = df_label_select,
      aes(label = Annotation),
      size = 3,
      max.overlaps = 50,
      force = 1.5,              # increase spread (default = 1)
      force_pull = 0.1,       # optional: keep labels closer to origin
      box.padding = 0.5,      # space around label box
      point.padding = 0.2,    # space around data point
      min.segment.length = 0  # always draw connector
    )

    ggsave(
      filename = file.path(out_dir, paste0("iN_vs_iDA_bubble_", g, ".pdf")),
      plot = p, width = 5, height = 5, device = cairo_pdf
    )
  }
}

  corr_mat = org_corr_mat,
  annot_class_df = annotation_to_class_corrgeno,
  annot_colors = annotation_class_colors_corrgeno,
  gene_count_df = gene_count_df,
  out_dir = out_dir_d50_CrossCorr_bubble
)
```

# Peroxisomal Abundance Evaluation
```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------- #
# Peroxisomal proteome: log2FC heatmap
# combined (all KOs) and split (iN / iDA)
# row annotation = peroxisomal subcellular location
# -------------------------------------------------- #

library(RColorBrewer)

# --- Step 1: Load peroxisome gene list with subcellular annotations
# adjust path if the file is stored elsewhere
perox_file <- "/Users/felix/Desktop/ppi_cowork/peroxisome_genes_loc.csv"
perox_raw <- read.csv(perox_file, header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# --- Step 2: Extract first gene symbol from "Gene Names" (space-separated)
# handle trailing-space column name introduced by read.csv ("Subcellular.location.")
subcell_col <- grep("Subcellular", colnames(perox_raw), value = TRUE)[1]

perox_annot <- perox_raw %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Genes            = trimws(sub(" .*", "", Gene.Names)),
    PeroxAnnotation  = trimws(.data[[subcell_col]])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Genes != "") %>%
  dplyr::select(Genes, PeroxAnnotation) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Genes, .keep_all = TRUE)

# --- Step 3: Filter log2FC_d50_annotated for peroxisomal genes
# KO columns are those ending in _iDA or _iN
ko_cols_perox <- grep("_(iDA|iN)$", colnames(log2FC_d50_annotated), value = TRUE)

perox_log2fc <- log2FC_d50_annotated %>%
  dplyr::filter(Genes %in% perox_annot$Genes) %>%
  dplyr::select(Genes, all_of(ko_cols_perox)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(perox_annot, by = "Genes")

# --- Step 4: Build log2FC matrix (rows = genes, cols = KOs); NA -> 0
perox_mat <- perox_log2fc %>%
  dplyr::select(Genes, all_of(ko_cols_perox)) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("Genes") %>%
  as.matrix()

perox_mat[is.na(perox_mat)] <- 0

# --- Step 5: Row annotation (one color bar for three peroxisomal subcategories)
row_ann_perox <- perox_log2fc %>%
  dplyr::select(Genes, PeroxAnnotation) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("Genes")

# ensure row order matches matrix
row_ann_perox <- row_ann_perox[rownames(perox_mat), , drop = FALSE]

perox_colors <- c(
  "Peroxisome"          = "#4DAF4A",
  "Peroxisome Matrix"   = "#984EA3",
  "Peroxisome Membrane" = "#FF7F00"
)

# --- Step 6: Column annotation for iN / iDA cell type
col_ann_perox <- data.frame(
  CellType = ifelse(grepl("_iDA$", ko_cols_perox), "iDA", "iN"),
  row.names = ko_cols_perox
)

celltype_colors_perox <- c(iDA = "grey80", iN = "grey40")

ann_colors_full_perox <- list(
  PeroxAnnotation = perox_colors,
  CellType        = celltype_colors_perox
)


# --- Step 7a: Heatmap – all 46 KO columns combined
pdf(file.path(out_dir_d50_heatmaps, "peroxisome_log2fc_heatmap_all.pdf"),
    width = 14, height = 9, useDingbats = FALSE)
pheatmap::pheatmap(
  mat               = perox_mat,
  color             = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdYlBu")))(100),
  annotation_row    = row_ann_perox,
  annotation_col    = col_ann_perox,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors_full_perox,
  scale = "row",
  cluster_rows      = TRUE,
  cluster_cols      = TRUE,
  show_rownames     = TRUE,
  show_colnames     = TRUE,
  fontsize          = 6,
  cellheight = 8,
  cellwidth = 8,
  border_color      = NA,
  na_col            = "grey90",
  main              = "Peroxisomal Proteome, log2FC all KOs (day 50, z-scaled by row)"
)
dev.off()

 # source file for combined heatmap
readr::write_csv(
  perox_log2fc,
  file.path(out_dir_d50_heatmaps, "peroxisome_log2fc_heatmap_all_sourcedata.csv")
)


# --- Step 7b: Split heatmaps – iN and iDA separately
# function to subset by cell type, drop all-zero rows, and save
plot_perox_split_heatmap <- function(mat, row_ann, perox_colors, cell_type, out_dir) {

  # subset columns for this cell type
  cols_sub <- grep(paste0("_", cell_type, "$"), colnames(mat), value = TRUE)
  mat_sub  <- mat[, cols_sub, drop = FALSE]

  # remove genes with all zeros (not detected in this cell type)
  mat_sub <- mat_sub[rowSums(mat_sub != 0, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, , drop = FALSE]

  # match row annotation to remaining genes
  row_ann_sub <- row_ann[rownames(mat_sub), , drop = FALSE]

  pdf(file.path(out_dir, paste0("peroxisome_log2fc_heatmap_", cell_type, ".pdf")),
      width = 9, height = 9, useDingbats = FALSE)
  pheatmap::pheatmap(
    mat               = mat_sub,
    color             = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdYlBu")))(100),
    annotation_row    = row_ann_sub,
    annotation_colors = list(PeroxAnnotation = perox_colors),
    scale = "row", 
    cluster_rows      = TRUE,
    cluster_cols      = TRUE,
    show_rownames     = TRUE,
    show_colnames     = TRUE,
    fontsize          = 6,
    border_color      = NA,
    cellheight = 8,
    cellwidth = 8,
    na_col            = "grey90",
    main              = paste0("Peroxisomal Proteome, log2FC ", cell_type, " (day 50, z-scaled by row)")
  )
  dev.off()

  # source file
  readr::write_csv(
    as.data.frame(mat_sub) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("Genes"),
    file.path(out_dir, paste0("peroxisome_log2fc_heatmap_", cell_type, "_sourcedata.csv"))
  )
}

plot_perox_split_heatmap(perox_mat, row_ann_perox, perox_colors, "iN",  out_dir_d50_heatmaps)
plot_perox_split_heatmap(perox_mat, row_ann_perox, perox_colors, "iDA", out_dir_d50_heatmaps)




# -------------------------------------------------- #
# Sorted heatmap: mean log2FC per annotation group
# rows = 4 groups (All, Peroxisome, Matrix, Membrane)
# cols = KOs sorted by "All Peroxisomal" mean
# no z-scaling; raw mean log2FC per group
# -------------------------------------------------- #

# --- Step 8: Define groups and compute mean log2FC per group per KO
# "All Peroxisomal" = mean across all peroxisomal genes in the matrix
perox_groups <- list(
  "All Peroxisomal"     = rownames(perox_mat),
  "Peroxisome"          = perox_annot %>% dplyr::filter(PeroxAnnotation == "Peroxisome")          %>% pull(Genes),
  "Peroxisome Matrix"   = perox_annot %>% dplyr::filter(PeroxAnnotation == "Peroxisome Matrix")   %>% pull(Genes),
  "Peroxisome Membrane" = perox_annot %>% dplyr::filter(PeroxAnnotation == "Peroxisome Membrane") %>% pull(Genes)
)

# result: matrix of shape groups x KOs
avg_perox_mat <- t(sapply(perox_groups, function(g) {
  sub_mat <- perox_mat[rownames(perox_mat) %in% g, , drop = FALSE]
  colMeans(sub_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
}))

# --- Step 9: Annotation for rows and columns
# row annotation: grey30 for "All", existing perox_colors for subcategories
perox_colors_avg <- c("All Peroxisomal" = "grey30", perox_colors)

row_ann_avg <- data.frame(

)


# --- Step 10b: Split heatmaps – iN and iDA, each sorted independently by "All Peroxisomal"
plot_perox_avg_split <- function(avg_mat, row_ann, ann_colors, cell_type, out_dir) {

  # subset to this cell type and sort by "All Peroxisomal"
  cols_ct <- grep(paste0("_", cell_type, "$"), colnames(avg_mat), value = TRUE)
  mat_ct  <- avg_mat[, cols_ct, drop = FALSE]
  mat_ct  <- mat_ct[, order(mat_ct["All Peroxisomal", ]), drop = FALSE]

  col_ann_ct <- data.frame(
    CellType  = rep(cell_type, ncol(mat_ct)),
    row.names = colnames(mat_ct)
  )

  pdf(file.path(out_dir, paste0("peroxisome_avg_log2fc_heatmap_", cell_type, ".pdf")),
      width = 9, height = 4, useDingbats = FALSE)
  pheatmap::pheatmap(
    mat               = mat_ct,
    color             = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdYlBu")))(100),
    annotation_row    = row_ann,
    annotation_col    = col_ann_ct,
    annotation_colors = ann_colors,
    cluster_rows      = FALSE,
    cluster_cols      = FALSE,
    show_rownames     = TRUE,
    show_colnames     = TRUE,
    fontsize          = 6,
    cellheight        = 8,
    cellwidth         = 8,
    border_color      = NA,
    na_col            = "grey90",
    main              = paste0("Mean log2FC per Peroxisomal Annotation Group ", cell_type, " (sorted by All, day 50)")
  )
  dev.off()

  readr::write_csv(
    as.data.frame(mat_ct) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("AnnotationGroup"),
    file.path(out_dir, paste0("peroxisome_avg_log2fc_heatmap_", cell_type, "_sourcedata.csv"))
  )
}

plot_perox_avg_split(avg_perox_mat, row_ann_avg, ann_colors_avg, "iN",  out_dir_d50_heatmaps)
plot_perox_avg_split(avg_perox_mat, row_ann_avg, ann_colors_avg, "iDA", out_dir_d50_heatmaps)





# -------------------------------------------------- #
# GO analysis on peroxisomal proteins per KO
# threshold: log2FC >= 0.5 (enriched) or <= -0.5 (de-enriched)
# min 5 genes required per direction to run GO
# background: all genes in log2FC_d50_annotated
# ontologies: BP, MF
# -------------------------------------------------- #
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)

# output directory for peroxisomal GO results
out_dir_d50_perox_GO <- file.path(dirname(out_dir_d50_heatmaps), "perox_GO")
dir.create(out_dir_d50_perox_GO, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# background: all unique gene symbols measured in the dataset
bg_genes_perox_GO <- unique(log2FC_d50_annotated$Genes)

# function: run GO for one gene set, save dotplot + source CSV per ontology
run_go_perox <- function(gene_set, background, label, out_dir, n_min = 5) {

  # skip if too few genes to run a meaningful enrichment
  if (length(gene_set) < n_min) {
    message("Skipping ", label, " – ", length(gene_set), " genes (min = ", n_min, ")")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  for (ont in c("BP", "MF")) {
    ego <- clusterProfiler::enrichGO(
      gene          = gene_set,
      universe      = background,
      OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db,
      keyType       = "SYMBOL",
      ont           = ont,
      pAdjustMethod = "BH",
      pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
      qvalueCutoff  = 0.2,
      readable      = TRUE
    )

    if (is.null(ego) || nrow(as.data.frame(ego)) == 0) {
      message("No GO ", ont, " results for: ", label)
      next
    }

    # save full result table
    readr::write_csv(
      as.data.frame(ego),
      file.path(out_dir, paste0("GO_perox_", ont, "_", label, "_sourcedata.csv"))
    )

    # dotplot: size = gene count, color = blue gradient for p.adjust
    p <- clusterProfiler::dotplot(ego, showCategory = 20, font.size = 6) +
      scale_color_gradient(low = "dodgerblue4", high = "lightblue", name = "p.adjust") +
      labs(title = paste0("GO ", ont, " | ", label, "  (|log2FC| \u2265 0.5)")) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 6) +
      theme(
        panel.grid  = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5)
      )

    ggsave(
      file.path(out_dir, paste0("GO_perox_", ont, "_", label, "_dotplot.pdf")),
      p, width = 6, height = 5, device = cairo_pdf
    )
  }
}

# loop over all 46 KO columns
# perox_log2fc retains original NA values (NA -> 0 was only applied to perox_mat)
# filtering for !is.na ensures 0-imputed values do not contribute
for (ko in ko_cols_perox) {

  ko_vals <- perox_log2fc %>%
    dplyr::select(Genes, all_of(ko)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[ko]]))

  genes_up <- ko_vals %>% dplyr::filter(.data[[ko]] >=  0.5) %>% pull(Genes)
  genes_dn <- ko_vals %>% dplyr::filter(.data[[ko]] <= -0.5) %>% pull(Genes)

  run_go_perox(genes_up, bg_genes_perox_GO, paste0(ko, "_enriched"),   out_dir_d50_perox_GO)
  run_go_perox(genes_dn, bg_genes_perox_GO, paste0(ko, "_deenriched"), out_dir_d50_perox_GO)
}
```

```{r}
SphMut_samples <- c("Ctrl_iN", "Ctrl_iDA", "GLB1_iN", "GLB1_iDA", "GBA1_iN", "GBA1_iDA", 
                    "ASAH1_iN", "ASAH1_iDA", "SMPD1_iN", "SMPD1_iDA", "PSAP_iN", "PSAP_iDA", 
                    "HEXA_iN", "HEXA_iDA", "HEXB_iN", "HEXB_iDA")


# --- Step 2. Subset and pivot
SphMut_df <- clean_d50_transformed_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(sample_id %in% SphMut_samples, day == 50)

    values_from = c(log2_fold_change, mean_ctrl, mean_ko, neg_log10_q_value, neg_log10_p_value),

    ),
    values_fn = list(

      mean_ctrl = mean,
      mean_ko = mean,

      neg_log10_p_value = mean
    )
  )


# --- Step 3. Add annotations
```

```{r}
    tibble(KO = ko, Organelle = ann, r = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value)
  })
})
```

## Correlation: All organelle annotations
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------- #
# Sph mutant investigation  
# Cross-correlation matrix of Sph-genotypes for each organelle
# --------------------------------------------------- #

# --- Step 1. Setup 
out_corr_dir <- file.path(out_dir_d50_SphMut, "Organelle_CrossCorr")
dir.create(out_corr_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

SphMut_sample_cols <- grep("log2_fold_change$", names(SphMut_annotated_df), value = TRUE)
SphMut_ko_type <- data.frame(CellType = ifelse(grepl("iDA", SphMut_sample_cols), "iDA", "iN"))
rownames(SphMut_ko_type) <- SphMut_sample_cols
celltype_colors <- c(iDA = "grey80", iN = "grey40")


# --- Step 2. Function: Compute KO×KO correlation matrix for a given organelle ---
plot_sphmut_corr_matrix <- function(organelle_name, df = SphMut_annotated_df) {
  gene_filter <- df[[organelle_name]] == 1
  mat <- df[gene_filter, SphMut_sample_cols, drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(mat) < 5) return(NULL)

  corr_mat <- cor(mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")
  corr_mat[!is.finite(corr_mat)] <- 0

  pheatmap::pheatmap(
    corr_mat,
    main = organelle_name,
    color = rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(11, "RdYlBu")),
    silent = TRUE,
    cellheight = 10,
    cellwidth = 10,
    na_col = "grey90",
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    border_color = NA,
    fontsize = 6,
    annotation_row = SphMut_ko_type,
    annotation_colors = list(CellType = celltype_colors)
  )
}


# --- Step 3. Run for all selected organelles 
selected_annotations <- c("Mito","MitoIMS","MitoMatrix","MitoMIM","MitoMOM","OXPHOS","mtComplexI","Golgi","Lysosome"      ,"ER","Cytoplasm","Nucleus","Autophagy","SynGO","Endo_iN_curated_Hundley","SynapseSVs","Presynaptic","Postsynaptic","NeuroDev","EndoLyso","EarlyEndosome","RecyclingEndosome","SVfusion","Svendocytosis","Svexocytosis")
  


# selected_annotations <- c("EndoLyso", "SynGO", "Endo_iN_curated_Hundley",
#                           "Lysosome", "Presynaptic", "Postsynaptic","SVfusion","Svendocytosis", "Svexocytosis")


valid_annotations <- intersect(selected_annotations, colnames(SphMut_annotated_df))
SphMut_ko_corr_hms <- lapply(valid_annotations, plot_sphmut_corr_matrix)

# SphMut_ko_corr_hms <- lapply(selected_annotations, plot_sphmut_corr_matrix)
# SphMut_ko_corr_hms <- Filter(Negate(is.null), SphMut_ko_corr_hms)


# --- Step 4. Save multi-panel heatmap PDF 
pdf(file.path(out_corr_dir, "SphMut_KOxKO_Corr_Heatmaps.pdf"), width = 30, height = 30, useDingbats = FALSE)
gridExtra::grid.arrange(
  grobs = lapply(SphMut_ko_corr_hms, `[[`, "gtable"),
  ncol = 4
)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
# ---  Define annotations of interest
annotation_cols_all <- c("SynGO","SynapseSVs",
  "Presynaptic", "Postsynaptic", "EarlyEndosome",
  "RecyclingEndosome", "Svendocytosis", "Svexocytosis", "vATPase"
)

# --- Helper function to reshape and summarize
prep_plot_data <- function(df, celltype) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::select(Gene, starts_with(paste0("log2FC_", celltype)), all_of(annotation_cols_all)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = starts_with(paste0("log2FC_", celltype)), names_to = "Time", values_to = "log2FC") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Time = str_extract(Time, "d\\d+")) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = all_of(annotation_cols_all), names_to = "Annotation", values_to = "in_group") %>%
    dplyr::filter(in_group == TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Time, Annotation) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      mean_log2FC = mean(log2FC, na.rm = TRUE),
      sem_log2FC = sd(log2FC, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# --- Prepare data for iN and iDA

plot_data_iDA <- prep_plot_data(asah1_ctrl_d233050_wide_df, "iDA")

# --- Color mapping
timeline_colors <- c(d50 = "dodgerblue3", d30 = "lightblue", d23 = "grey70")

# --- Plot function
plot_bar <- function(data, title) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = Time, y = mean_log2FC, fill = Time)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", width = 0.7, linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_log2FC - sem_log2FC, ymax = mean_log2FC + sem_log2FC),
                  width = 0.2) +
    facet_wrap(~Annotation, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = timeline_colors) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 6) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    ) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Timepoint", y = "Mean log2FC")
}

# --- Plot iN and iDA separately
plot_iN_ASAH1Timecomp <- plot_bar(plot_data_iN, "ASAH1 vs Ctrl – iN Neurons")
plot_iDA_ASAH1Timecomp  <- plot_bar(plot_data_iDA, "ASAH1 vs Ctrl – iDA Neurons")

print(plot_iDA_ASAH1Timecomp)
```

# Euler plot for overlap of annotations of genotypes
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------------- #
# Euler plot of downregulated genes across genotypes
# within user-defined subcellular annotations (e.g. MitoMatrix).
# --------------------------------------------------------- #
library(tidyverse)
library(eulerr)

# --- 1. Define Parameters
#annotations_to_check <- c("MitoMatrix","OXPHOS","Mito") 
annotations_to_check <- c("OXPHOS")       
logfc_thresh <- -0.75                         
genotypes <- c("ASAH1", "GBA1", "SMPD1", 
               "HEXA", "HEXB", "PSAP")        


# --- 2. Function to extract downregulated gene sets
# For each genotype and cell type (iN or iDA), extract genes that are:
# (a) downregulated below threshold, AND
# (b) annotated with at least one of the selected annotations
get_down_genes_by_annotation <- function(celltype, df, annotations, fc_thresh) {
  gene_sets <- list()
  for (g in genotypes) {
    fc_col <- paste0(g, "_", celltype, "_d50_log2_fold_change")
    if (!fc_col %in% colnames(df)) next

    down_genes <- df %>%
      filter(!!sym(fc_col) < fc_thresh)

    gene_set <- annotations %>%
      map(~ filter(down_genes, !!sym(.x) == 1) %>% pull(Genes)) %>%
      unlist() %>%
      unique()

    gene_sets[[paste0(g, "_", celltype)]] <- gene_set
  }
  return(gene_sets)
}


# --- 3. Extract gene sets for iN and iDA 
gene_sets_iN  <- get_down_genes_by_annotation("iN",  SphMut_annotated_df, annotations_to_check, logfc_thresh)
gene_sets_iDA <- get_down_genes_by_annotation("iDA", SphMut_annotated_df, annotations_to_check, logfc_thresh)


# --- 4. Fit and plot Euler diagrams 
fit_iN  <- euler(gene_sets_iN)
fit_iDA <- euler(gene_sets_iDA)

# Save iN plot
pdf(file.path(out_dir_d50_SphMuteuler, "Euler_iN_downregulated_all_OXPHOS.pdf"), width = 8, height = 8)
plot(fit_iN,
     fills = list(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.4),
     labels = list(font = 1),
     main = "iN: Overlap of Downregulated Genes in OXPHOS")
dev.off()

# Save iDA plot
pdf(file.path(out_dir_d50_SphMuteuler, "Euler_iDA_downregulated_all_OXPHOS.pdf"), width = 8, height = 8)
plot(fit_iDA,
     fills = list(fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.4),
     labels = list(font = 1),
     main = "iDA: Overlap of Downregulated Genes in OXPHOS")
dev.off()


# --- 5. Export list of hits as long-format CSV 
# Convert gene set list to tidy long table
make_hit_table <- function(gene_sets_list, celltype) {
  enframe(gene_sets_list, name = "Label", value = "Genes") %>%
    unnest(Genes) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Genotype  = str_extract(Label, "^[^_]+"),
      CellType  = celltype,
      Annotation = paste(annotations_to_check, collapse = ";")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Gene = Genes, Annotation, CellType, Genotype)
}

hits_iN  <- make_hit_table(gene_sets_iN, "iN")
hits_iDA <- make_hit_table(gene_sets_iDA, "iDA")
hits_all <- bind_rows(hits_iN, hits_iDA)

# --- 6. Write to CSV
write_csv(hits_all, file.path(out_dir_d50_SphMuteuler, "Downregulated_OXPHOS_hits_by_genotype.csv"))

# --- 7. Pairwise overlap matrix (gene counts)
all_sets <- c(gene_sets_iN, gene_sets_iDA)
set_names <- names(all_sets)

overlap_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(all_sets), ncol = length(all_sets),
                         dimnames = list(set_names, set_names))

for (i in seq_along(all_sets)) {
  for (j in seq_along(all_sets)) {
    overlap_matrix[i, j] <- length(intersect(all_sets[[i]], all_sets[[j]]))
  }
}

# Convert to dataframe and write
overlap_df <- as.data.frame(overlap_matrix) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Genotype")

write_csv(overlap_df, file.path(out_dir_d50_SphMuteuler, "Pairwise_overlap_counts_OXPHOS.csv"))




```

```{r}
## -- loop function 
library(tidyverse)
library(limma)

# Define genotypes of interest
genotype_set <- c("GBA1", "ASAH1", "HEXA", "HEXB", "SMPD1", "PSAP")

# Initialize results list
pairwise_results <- list()

# Extract iDA-only metadata
sample_info_iDA <- tibble(sample_id = colnames(SphMut_mat)) %>%
  mutate(
    Genotype = str_extract(sample_id, "^[^_]+"),
    Neuron = case_when(
      grepl("_iDA_", sample_id) ~ "iDA",
      grepl("_iN_", sample_id) ~ "iN",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Neuron), Neuron == "iDA", Genotype %in% genotype_set)

# Loop over all genotype pairs
for (pair in combn(genotype_set, 2, simplify = FALSE)) {
  g1 <- pair[1]
  g2 <- pair[2]
  label <- paste0(g1, "_vs_", g2)

  # Subset metadata
  sub_info <- sample_info_iDA %>%
    filter(Genotype %in% c(g1, g2)) %>%
    mutate(Genotype = factor(Genotype, levels = c(g2, g1)))  # g2 is baseline

  # Subset matrix
  sub_mat <- SphMut_mat[, sub_info$sample_id]

  # Design and model
  design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + Genotype, data = sub_info)
  colnames(design) <- levels(sub_info$Genotype)

  fit <- lmFit(sub_mat, design)
  contrast <- makeContrasts(contrast = paste0(g1, "-", g2), levels = design)
  fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrast)
  fit2 <- eBayes(fit2)

  # Extract top genes
  top_genes <- topTable(fit2, coef = "contrast", number = Inf) %>%
    rownames_to_column("Gene") %>%
    mutate(Comparison = label)

  # Store
  pairwise_results[[label]] <- top_genes
}

# Combine all results into a single dataframe
all_pairwise_df <- bind_rows(pairwise_results)
```

# GRN d30/50 DA neuron investigation
we see that the DA neurons of GRN in both day 30 and day50 have differences in their proteome compared to the other genotypes or the iN of the same genotype

- make dataframe of only Ctrl, GRN, GBA1, ASAH1, SMPD1 for day30 and day 50; both iN and iDA
- add annotations to Genes in dataframe
- also calculate the log2FC but also keep the mean_ctrl and mean_ko values in the dataframe => calculate mean of that 

- plot mean_ctrl and mean_ko across the genotypes
- make heatmap containing both timepoints => gene.rows are matched
- plot corr of GRN/Ctrl day30 (x) and GRN/Ctrl day50 (y)
- plot outliers of this corr and see what is different? 

```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------- #
# GRN d30/50 DA neuron investigation  
# Cross-correlation matrix of Sph-genotypes for each organelle
# --------------------------------------------------- #

# --- Step 1. use modified function to loop through clean_50_transformed_df to get genotypes and days and annotations in new dataframe 
process_day_data_combined <- function(df, binary_matrix) {
  selected_samples <- c("Ctrl_iN", "Ctrl_iDA", "GRN_iN", "GRN_iDA", 
                        "GBA1_iN", "GBA1_iDA", "ASAH1_iN", "ASAH1_iDA", 
                        "SMPD1_iN", "SMPD1_iDA")
  
  # Filter to relevant samples only
  df_filtered <- df %>% filter(sample_id %in% selected_samples, day %in% c(30, 50))
  
  # Add time label to sample_id (to avoid collision after pivoting)
  df_filtered <- df_filtered %>%
    mutate(sample_id = paste0(sample_id, "_d", day))
  
  # Pivot to wide format
  complete_data <- df_filtered %>%
    dplyr::select(Genes, sample_id, log2_fold_change, mean_ctrl, mean_ko, neg_log10_q_value, neg_log10_p_value) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = sample_id,
      values_from = c(log2_fold_change, mean_ctrl, mean_ko, neg_log10_q_value, neg_log10_p_value),
      names_glue = "{sample_id}_{.value}",
      values_fill = list(
        log2_fold_change = 0, mean_ctrl = 0, mean_ko = 0,
        neg_log10_q_value = 0, neg_log10_p_value = 0
      ),
      values_fn = list(
        log2_fold_change = sum,
        mean_ctrl = mean,
        mean_ko = mean,
        neg_log10_q_value = mean,
        neg_log10_p_value = mean
      )
    )
  
  # Add annotations
  complete_data_annotated <- complete_data %>%
    left_join(binary_matrix, by = "Genes") %>%
    replace(is.na(.), 0)
  
  return(complete_data_annotated)
}

# --- Step 2. Save day 30 and day50 data as csv file 
day3050_subset <- process_day_data_combined(clean_d50_transformed_df, binary_matrix)
write.csv(day3050_subset, file=file.path(out_dir_d50_GRN, "diff132_day3050_subset.csv"),row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(day3050_subset, file=file.path(out_dir_d50_dataframes, "diff132_day3050_subset.csv"),row.names = FALSE)



# --------------------------------------------------- #
# GRN d30/50 DA neuron investigation  
# heatmap of day30/50 dataset
# --------------------------------------------------- #

# --- Step 3. Function for Heatmap plotting
generate_day3050_heatmap <- function(df, title_label = "Combined Heatmap") {
  # Extract log2FC columns
  log2fc_cols <- grep("_log2_fold_change$", names(df), value = TRUE)
  mat <- as.matrix(df[, log2fc_cols])
  rownames(mat) <- df$Genes
  storage.mode(mat) <- "numeric"
  mat[!is.finite(mat)] <- 0

  # Remove invariant rows/columns
  mat <- mat[apply(mat, 1, var) != 0, , drop = FALSE]
  mat <- mat[, apply(mat, 2, var) != 0, drop = FALSE]

  # Sample annotation: extract genotype, neuron type, and day
  sample_info <- data.frame(
    sample_id = colnames(mat)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Genotype = str_extract(sample_id, "^[^_]+"),
      Neuron = str_extract(sample_id, "_iDA|_iN") %>% str_remove("^_"),
      Day = str_extract(sample_id, "_d\\d+") %>% str_remove("^_")
    ) %>%
    column_to_rownames("sample_id")

  # Annotation colors
  ann_colors <- list(
    Genotype = setNames(brewer.pal(length(unique(sample_info$Genotype)), "Set1"), unique(sample_info$Genotype)),
    Neuron = setNames(c("grey40", "grey70"), unique(sample_info$Neuron)),
    Day = setNames(c("#3182bd", "#9ecae1"), unique(sample_info$Day))
  )

  # Generate heatmap
  pheatmap::pheatmap(
    mat,
    scale = "row",
    color = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(n = 11, name = "RdYlBu")))(100),
    annotation_col = sample_info,
    annotation_colors = ann_colors,
    breaks = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 101),
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    show_rownames = FALSE,
    show_colnames = TRUE,
    use_raster = FALSE,
    #angle_col = 90,
    main = title_label,
    fontsize = 10,
    border_color = NA
  )
}

# --- Step 4. call function
day3050_heatmap <- generate_day3050_heatmap(day3050_subset, title_label = "LSD DA Neuron Log2FC – Day30 & Day50")
#day3050_heatmap


# --- Step 5. save heatmap as pdf in both dirs
pdf(file.path(out_dir_d50_heatmaps, "diff132_selectKO_day3050_heatmap.pdf"), width = 8, height = 10, useDingbats = FALSE)
generate_day3050_heatmap(day3050_subset, title_label = "LSD DA Neuron Log2FC – Day30 & Day50")
dev.off()

pdf(file.path(out_dir_d50_GRN, "diff132_selectKO_day3050_heatmap.pdf"), width = 8, height = 10, useDingbats = FALSE)

# --------------------------------------------------- #
# GRN d30/50 DA neuron investigation  
# Correlation scatterplot of day30 / day 50 DA GRN neurons
# --------------------------------------------------- #

# --- Step 6. Color & facet~wrap by annotation of compartment 
# Create a copy to avoid modifying original
annot_subset <- day3050_subset


# --- Step 7. define protein sub cellular localizations --- 
# Step 7a: Identify annotation columns (logical columns at the end of the dataframe)
annotation_columns <- names(annot_subset)[sapply(annot_subset, is.logical)]

# Step 7b: Remove overly specific or problematic annotations
usable_annotations <- setdiff(annotation_columns, c("Autophagy_det", "EndoDetailLoac"))

# Step 7c: Reshape to long format: Gene - Localization pairs
annotation_long <- annot_subset %>%
  dplyr::select(Genes, all_of(usable_annotations)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -Genes, names_to = "Localization", values_to = "Present") %>%
  filter(Present) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Present) %>%
  distinct()


# --- Step 8. define protein sub cellular localizations --- 
# Step 8a: Create full combination of genes and facet localizations
facet_levels <- unique(annotation_long$Localization)

# Step 8c: Expand gene-localization combinations
facet_expanded <- expand.grid(
  Genes = unique(annotation_long$Genes),
```

## Annotation-based corr heatmaps
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------- #

disease_classes <- list(

  Neuronal.ceroid.lipofuscinoses = c("PPT1", "CTSD", "GRN", "ATP13A2", "CTSF", "KCTD7", "TPP1", "CLN3", "DNAJC5", "CLN5", "CLN6", "MFSD8", "CLN8"),
  Integral.membrane.protein.disorders = c("ATP13A2", "CLN3", "CTNS", "LAMP2", "MCOLN1", "NPC1", "NPC2", "SCARB2", "SLC17A5"),
  Lipid.storage.diseases = c("GAA", "LIPA")
)

  Sphingolipidoses = "#D53E4F",

)
disease_class_df <- enframe(disease_classes) %>% unnest(value) %>% dplyr::rename(KO = value, DiseaseClass = name)


# --- Step 2. Add Disease Class to subdataframe, reshape and join back annotations

  dplyr::select(Genes, matches("_iN_log2_fold_change$|_iDA_log2_fold_change$")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -Genes, names_to = "sample", values_to = "log2fc") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    sample = str_remove(sample, "_log2_fold_change$"),
    KO = str_extract(sample, "^[^_]+"),
    celltype = str_extract(sample, "(iN|iDA)$"),
    log2fc = as.numeric(log2fc)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(disease_class_df, by = "KO") %>%
  distinct(Genes, sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(Genes, KO, DiseaseClass), names_from = sample, values_from = log2fc)

# Add annotation columns back in

  "mtComplexI", "Golgi", "Lysosome", "ER", "Cytoplasm", "Nucleus",
  "Autophagy", "SynGO", "Endo_iN_curated_Hundley", "SynapseSVs",
  "Presynaptic", "Postsynaptic", "NeuroDev", "EndoLyso", "EarlyEndosome",
  "RecyclingEndosome", "SVfusion", "Svendocytosis", "Svexocytosis", "vATPase"
)

annotated_log2fc_df <- annotated_log2fc_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    complete_data_annotated_day50 %>% dplyr::select(Genes, all_of(annotation_cols_all)),
    by = "Genes"
  )


# --- Step 3. Save the annotated dataframe
write.csv(annotated_log2fc_df, file = file.path(out_dir_d50_DisClass, "Annotated_Log2FC_with_DiseaseClass.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


# --- Step 4. Define correlation and plotting function by annotations
plot_annotation_correlation <- function(annot_df, annotation_cols, out_dir, cellsize = 10) {
  # Calculate average profile per annotation
  annotation_means <- map_dfc(annotation_cols, function(annot_col) {
    genes <- annot_df %>% filter(.data[[annot_col]] == 1) %>% pull(Genes)
    sub <- annot_df %>% filter(Genes %in% genes) %>% dplyr::select(matches("_(iN|iDA)$"))
    colMeans(sub, na.rm = TRUE)
  })
  colnames(annotation_means) <- annotation_cols
  annotation_cor <- cor(annotation_means, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
  
  # Save correlation matrix
  write.csv(annotation_cor, file = file.path(out_dir, "CustomAnnotation_CorrMatrix.csv"))
  
  # Create annotation bar
  annotation_df <- data.frame(DiseaseClass = colnames(annotation_cor)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(annotation_cols %>% enframe(name = NULL, value = "Annotation"), by = c("DiseaseClass" = "Annotation")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(DiseaseClass = factor(DiseaseClass, levels = names(disease_colors)))
  
  row_annot <- data.frame(DiseaseClass = factor(rep(names(disease_colors), length.out = ncol(annotation_cor)), levels = names(disease_colors)))
  rownames(row_annot) <- colnames(annotation_cor)

  # Plot heatmap
  pdf(file = file.path(out_dir, "CustomAnnotation_AnnotationCorrHeatmap.pdf"), width = 8, height = 8)
  pheatmap::pheatmap(
    annotation_cor,
    color = colorRampPalette(rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n = 11, name = "RdYlBu")))(100),
    annotation_row = row_annot,
    annotation_colors = list(DiseaseClass = disease_colors),
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    fontsize = 6,
    cellheight = 8,
    cellwidth  = 8,
    border = NA
  )
  dev.off()
}
```

## Annotation-based Circos of correlations
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------- #
# Disease-class-based comparison day50  
# Correlations between KO conditions
# --------------------------------------------------- #
library(circlize)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(tidyverse)
library(grid)

cor_threshold <- 0.6

# --- Step 1. Define color mappings for plotting
neuron_colors <- c("iN" = "dodgerblue", "iDA" = "#D53E4F")
# disease_colors <- c(
#   Sphingolipidoses = "#D53E4F",
#   Neuronal.ceroid.lipofuscinoses = "#FEE08B",
#   Integral.membrane.protein.disorders = "#E6F598",
#   Lipid.storage.diseases = "#66C2A5"
# )

# Step 1. Expand to sample-level keys
disease_class_df <- enframe(disease_classes, name = "DiseaseClass", value = "KO") %>%
  unnest(KO) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DiseaseColor = disease_colors[DiseaseClass]) %>%
  crossing(CellType = c("iN", "iDA")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sample = paste0(KO, "_", CellType))


# --- Step 2. Set Annotations of interest, can corr threshold 
#custom_annotation_cols <- c("Mito", "EarlyEndosome","RecyclingEndosome", "SVfusion", "Svendocytosis", "Svexocytosis", "vATPase")
custom_annotation_cols <- c("Mito", "MitoIMS", "MitoMatrix", "MitoMIM", "MitoMOM", "OXPHOS",
                     "mtComplexI", "Golgi", "Lysosome", "ER", "Cytoplasm", "Nucleus",
                     "Autophagy", "SynGO", "Endo_iN_curated_Hundley", "SynapseSVs",
                     "Presynaptic", "Postsynaptic", "NeuroDev", "EndoLyso", "EarlyEndosome",
                     "RecyclingEndosome", "SVfusion", "Svendocytosis", "Svexocytosis", "vATPase")

# custom_annotation_cols <- c("Golgi", "Lysosome", "SynGO", "Endo_iN_curated_Hundley", "SynapseSVs",
#                      "Presynaptic", "Postsynaptic","EarlyEndosome",
#                      "RecyclingEndosome", "SVfusion", "Svendocytosis", "Svexocytosis", "vATPase")

min_genes_per_genotype <- 5


# --- Step 3. Loop through custom annotations, calculate correlations and save as csv file 
for (annot in custom_annotation_cols) {
  message("Processing annotation: ", annot)

  # Step 3.1: Filter for annotated genes
  annot_subset_df <- annotated_log2fc_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data[[annot]] == 1)

  # Step 3.2: Check valid samples with ≥3 annotated genes
  valid_samples <- annot_subset_df %>%
    dplyr::select(Genes, KO, DiseaseClass, matches("_(iN|iDA)$")) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = matches("_(iN|iDA)$"), names_to = "sample", values_to = "log2fc") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(sample) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(log2fc)) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(n_genes = n_distinct(Genes), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::filter(n_genes >= min_genes_per_genotype) %>%
    pull(sample)

  if (length(valid_samples) < 2) {
    warning("Skipping ", annot, ": not enough valid samples")
    next
  }

  # Step 3.3: Create filtered log2FC matrix
  log2fc_mat <- annot_subset_df %>%
    dplyr::select(Genes, all_of(valid_samples)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Genes) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    column_to_rownames("Genes") %>%
    as.matrix()

  # Step 3.4: Compute Pearson correlation
  corr_mat <- cor(log2fc_mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")

  # Step 3.5: Save matrix
  write.csv(corr_mat, file = file.path(out_dir_d50_DisClass_circos, paste0("CorrMatrix_", annot, ".csv")))

  # Step 3.6: Link table for circos
  corr_links <- expand.grid(from = rownames(corr_mat), to = colnames(corr_mat), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::filter(from != to) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pair_id = map2_chr(from, to, ~ paste(sort(c(.x, .y)), collapse = "_"))) %>%
    distinct(pair_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(correlation = mapply(function(x, y) corr_mat[x, y], from, to)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(abs(correlation) > cor_threshold)

  # Step 3.7: Save link table
  write.csv(corr_links, file = file.path(out_dir_d50_DisClass_circos, paste0("LinkTable_", annot, "_absCorr", cor_threshold, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
}


# --- Step 4. Define plotting function for Circos plot of Disease mutant correlations
plot_annotation_genotype_circos <- function(annot_df,annotation_cols,disease_class_df,out_dir,min_gene_n = min_genes_per_genotype,pos_thresh = 0.5,neg_thresh = -0.5) {
  for (annot in annotation_cols) {
    message("Processing annotation: ", annot)
    
    # Filter genes for the annotation
    genes <- annot_df %>% filter(.data[[annot]] == 1) %>% pull(Genes) %>% unique()
    sub_df <- annot_df %>% filter(Genes %in% genes)

    # Make gene × genotype matrix
    mat_long <- sub_df %>%
      dplyr::select(Genes, matches("_(iN|iDA)$")) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(-Genes, names_to = "sample", values_to = "log2fc") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(log2fc)) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(sample) %>%
      dplyr::filter(n() >= min_gene_n) %>%
      ungroup()

    mat_wide <- mat_long %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = log2fc) %>%
      column_to_rownames("Genes")

    if (ncol(mat_wide) < 2) {
      warning("Skipping: Not enough valid samples for ", annot)
      next
    }

    # Compute correlation
    cor_mat <- cor(mat_wide, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")

    # Save CSV
    write.csv(cor_mat, file = file.path(out_dir, paste0("CorrMatrix_", annot, ".csv")))

    # Make link table
    link_df <- expand.grid(from = colnames(cor_mat), to = colnames(cor_mat), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      dplyr::filter(from != to) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(pair_id = pmap_chr(list(from, to), ~ paste(sort(c(..1, ..2)), collapse = "_"))) %>%
      distinct(pair_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(correlation = mapply(function(x, y) cor_mat[x, y], from, to)) %>%
      dplyr::filter(correlation >= pos_thresh | correlation <= neg_thresh)

    if (nrow(link_df) == 0) {
      warning("Skipping: No links pass thresholds for ", annot)
      next
    }

    # Build sector metadata with deduplication
    sector_meta_df <- tibble(sample = colnames(cor_mat)) %>%
      dplyr::left_join(disease_class_df, by = "sample") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        DiseaseClass = replace_na(DiseaseClass, "Unassigned"),
        DiseaseColor = replace_na(DiseaseColor, "grey90")
      ) %>%
      distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE)
    
    # Lock sector order
    sectors <- sector_meta_df$sample
    
    # Build colors in strict sector order
    disease_class_colors <- setNames(sector_meta_df$DiseaseColor, sectors)[sectors]
    neuron_type_colors   <- setNames(neuron_colors[sector_meta_df$CellType], sectors)[sectors]
    
    # sanity check
    if (any(is.na(disease_class_colors))) {
      stop("Error: some sectors have no DiseaseColor mapping.")
    }

        # Save sectors and colors for debugging
        sector_colors_df <- tibble(sample = sectors, DiseaseColor = disease_class_colors[sectors],NeuronColor  = neuron_type_colors[sectors])

      write.csv(
        sector_colors_df,
        file = file.path(out_dir, paste0("SectorColors_", annot, ".csv")),
        row.names = FALSE
      )

    
    ## PlotCircos plot
    # Start PDF
    pdf(file.path(out_dir, paste0("Circos_", annot, ".pdf")), width = 10, height = 10)

    circos.clear()
    circos.par(start.degree = 90, gap.degree = 1)

    chordDiagram(
      link_df,
      order = as.character(sectors),
      grid.col = neuron_type_colors,
      col = alpha(colorRamp2(c(-1, 0, 1),
                             c("blue", "white", "red"))(link_df$correlation), 0.6),
      annotationTrack = "grid",
      transparency = 0,
      preAllocateTracks = list(
       # list(track.height = 0.05),  # Track 1: labels
        list(track.height = 0.03),  # Track 2: disease
        list(track.height = 0.03)   # Track 3: neuron
      )
    )
    
    # Labels
    circos.trackPlotRegion(track.index = 1, panel.fun = function(x, y) {
      sector_name <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
      circos.text(CELL_META$xcenter, CELL_META$ylim[1] + mm_y(1),
                  labels = sector_name,
                  facing = "clockwise", niceFacing = TRUE,
                  adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = 0.5)
    }, bg.border = NA)
    
   # after chordDiagram()
    actual_order <- get.all.sector.index()
    
    # Outer: disease
    circos.trackPlotRegion(
      track.index = 2,
      bg.col = disease_class_colors[match(actual_order, names(disease_class_colors))],
      panel.fun = function(x, y) {}, bg.border = NA
    )
    
    # Inner: neuron
    circos.trackPlotRegion(
      track.index = 3,
      bg.col = neuron_type_colors[match(actual_order, names(neuron_type_colors))],
      panel.fun = function(x, y) {}, bg.border = NA
    )

    # add legend
    draw(Legend(at = c(-1, 0, 1),col_fun = colorRamp2(c(-1, 0, 1), c("blue", "white", "red")),title = "Pearson r",direction = "horizontal",legend_width = unit(3, "cm")), x = unit(0.5, "npc"), y = unit(0.02, "npc"), just = c("center", "bottom"))
    draw(Legend(labels = names(neuron_colors), legend_gp = gpar(fill = neuron_colors), title = "Neuron Type"), x = unit(0.02, "npc"), y = unit(0.02, "npc"), just = c("left", "bottom"))
    draw(Legend(labels = names(disease_colors), legend_gp = gpar(fill = disease_colors), title = "Disease Class"), x = unit(1, "npc"), y = unit(0.02, "npc"), just = c("right", "bottom"))

    dev.off()
  }
}

# --- Step 5. Call function
plot_annotation_genotype_circos(
  annot_df = annotated_log2fc_df,
  annotation_cols = custom_annotation_cols,
  disease_class_df = disease_class_df,   
  out_dir = out_dir_d50_DisClass_circos,
  pos_thresh = 0.7,
  neg_thresh = -0.2
)
```

## Split Annotation-based Circos of correlations
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------- #
# Disease-class-based comparison day50  
# Correlations between KO conditions
# Split Circos by Positive/Negative Correlations
# --------------------------------------------------- #


# --- 1. Define Split Circos function 
plot_annotation_genotype_circos_split <- function(annot_df, annotation_cols, disease_class_df, out_dir,
                                                 min_gene_n = 5, pos_thresh = 0.7, neg_thresh = -0.3) {
  for (annot in annotation_cols) {
    message("Processing split circos for annotation: ", annot)

    # 1. Filter genes belonging to the current annotation
    genes <- annot_df %>% filter(.data[[annot]] == 1) %>% pull(Genes) %>% unique()
    sub_df <- annot_df %>% filter(Genes %in% genes)

    # 2. Build long-format matrix for valid samples
    mat_long <- sub_df %>%
      dplyr::select(Genes, matches("_(iN|iDA)$")) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(-Genes, names_to = "sample", values_to = "log2fc") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(log2fc)) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(sample) %>%
      dplyr::filter(n() >= min_gene_n) %>%
      ungroup()

    # 3. Pivot to wide format (Genes × samples)
    mat_wide <- mat_long %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = log2fc) %>%
      column_to_rownames("Genes")

    if (ncol(mat_wide) < 2) {
      warning("Skipping: Not enough valid samples for ", annot)
      next
    }

    # 4. Compute Pearson correlation
    cor_mat <- cor(mat_wide, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")

    # 5. Build link data frames for positive and negative correlations
    make_link_df <- function(thresh, sign) {
      df <- expand.grid(from = colnames(cor_mat), to = colnames(cor_mat), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
        dplyr::filter(from != to) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(pair_id = pmap_chr(list(from, to), ~ paste(sort(c(..1, ..2)), collapse = "_"))) %>%
        distinct(pair_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(correlation = mapply(function(x, y) cor_mat[x, y], from, to))
      if (sign == "pos") df %>% filter(correlation >= thresh) else df %>% filter(correlation <= thresh)
    }

    link_df_pos <- make_link_df(pos_thresh, "pos")
    link_df_neg <- make_link_df(neg_thresh, "neg")

    if (nrow(link_df_pos) == 0 & nrow(link_df_neg) == 0) {
      warning("Skipping: No links pass thresholds for ", annot)
      next
    }

    # 6. Build sector metadata with DiseaseClass and NeuronType
    sector_meta_df <- tibble(sample = colnames(cor_mat)) %>%
      dplyr::left_join(disease_class_df, by = "sample") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(DiseaseClass = replace_na(DiseaseClass, "Unassigned"),
             DiseaseColor = replace_na(DiseaseColor, "grey90")) %>%
      distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE)

    sectors <- sector_meta_df$sample
    disease_class_colors <- setNames(sector_meta_df$DiseaseColor, sectors)
    neuron_type_colors   <- setNames(neuron_colors[sector_meta_df$CellType], sectors)

    # 7. Helper for plotting circos (per correlation sign)
    make_chord <- function(link_df, suffix) {
      if (nrow(link_df) == 0) return(NULL)

      pdf(file.path(out_dir, paste0("Circos_", annot, "_", suffix, ".pdf")), width = 10, height = 10)
      circos.clear()
      circos.par(start.degree = 90, gap.degree = 1)

      chordDiagram(
        link_df,
        order = as.character(sectors),
        grid.col = neuron_type_colors,
        col = alpha(colorRamp2(c(-1, 0, 1), c("blue", "white", "red"))(link_df$correlation), 0.6),
        annotationTrack = "grid",
        transparency = 0,
        preAllocateTracks = list(
          #list(track.height = 0.05),  # 1: labels
          list(track.height = 0.03),  # 2: disease
          list(track.height = 0.03)   # 3: neuron
        )
      )

      # Reorder colors based on actual drawn sectors
      actual_order <- get.all.sector.index()
      sector_meta_ordered <- sector_meta_df %>%
        dplyr::filter(sample %in% actual_order) %>%
        dplyr::arrange(match(sample, actual_order))
      disease_class_colors_ordered <- sector_meta_ordered$DiseaseColor
      neuron_type_colors_ordered   <- neuron_colors[sector_meta_ordered$CellType]

      # Track 1: Labels
      circos.trackPlotRegion(track.index = 1, panel.fun = function(x, y) {
        sector_name <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
        circos.text(CELL_META$xcenter, CELL_META$ylim[1] + mm_y(1),
                    labels = sector_name,
                    facing = "clockwise", niceFacing = TRUE,
                    adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = 0.5)
      }, bg.border = NA)

      # Track 2: Disease class
      circos.trackPlotRegion(track.index = 2, bg.col = disease_class_colors_ordered,
                             panel.fun = function(x, y) {}, bg.border = NA)

      # Track 3: Neuron type
      circos.trackPlotRegion(track.index = 3, bg.col = neuron_type_colors_ordered,
                             panel.fun = function(x, y) {}, bg.border = NA)

      # Title
      grid.text(paste0("Genotype Correlation | ", annot, " | ", suffix),
                x = 0.5, y = 0.98, gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold"))

      # Legends
      draw(Legend(at = c(-1, 0, 1),
                  col_fun = colorRamp2(c(-1, 0, 1), c("blue", "white", "red")),
                  title = "Pearson r", direction = "horizontal",
                  legend_width = unit(3, "cm")),
           x = unit(0.5, "npc"), y = unit(0.02, "npc"), just = c("center", "bottom"))

      draw(Legend(labels = names(neuron_colors), legend_gp = gpar(fill = neuron_colors),
                  title = "Neuron Type"),
           x = unit(0.02, "npc"), y = unit(0.02, "npc"), just = c("left", "bottom"))

      draw(Legend(labels = names(disease_colors), legend_gp = gpar(fill = disease_colors),
                  title = "Disease Class"),
           x = unit(1, "npc"), y = unit(0.02, "npc"), just = c("right", "bottom"))

      dev.off()
    }

    # 8. Draw circos for positive and negative correlations
    make_chord(link_df_pos, "PositiveCorr")
    make_chord(link_df_neg, "NegativeCorr")
  }
}



# --- 2. Call function and define corr thresholds
plot_annotation_genotype_circos_split(
  annot_df = annotated_log2fc_df,
  annotation_cols = custom_annotation_cols,
  disease_class_df = disease_class_df,

  neg_thresh = -0.2
)



# detach Compelxhatmap, since it masks pheatmap for later
```

```{r}
# UMAP: proteins as points, 46 KO log2FC as features

#install.packages("uwot")
library(uwot)

# output directory
out_dir_d50_UMAP <- file.path(dirname(out_dir_d50_heatmaps), "UMAP")
dir.create(out_dir_d50_UMAP, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)


# --- Step 1: Build feature matrix (proteins × KO columns)
ko_cols_umap <- grep("_(iDA|iN)$", colnames(log2FC_d50_annotated), value = TRUE)

umap_feat_mat <- log2FC_d50_annotated %>%
  dplyr::select(Genes, all_of(ko_cols_umap)) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("Genes") %>%
  as.matrix()

# NA → 0
umap_feat_mat[is.na(umap_feat_mat)] <- 0

# remove proteins with zero variance (no information across KOs)
umap_feat_mat <- umap_feat_mat[apply(umap_feat_mat, 1, var) > 0, ]


# --- Step 2: UMAP embedding
set.seed(42)
umap_coords <- uwot::umap(umap_feat_mat, n_neighbors = 7, min_dist = 0.05,
                           spread = 2, metric = "euclidean")

umap_df <- data.frame(
  Genes = rownames(umap_feat_mat),
  UMAP1 = umap_coords[, 1],
  UMAP2 = umap_coords[, 2],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


# --- Step 3: Disease class mean log2FC per protein
# map genotype → disease class; first occurrence handles proteins in multiple classes
disease_class_map_umap <- utils::stack(disease_classes) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Genotype = values, DiseaseClass = ind) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DiseaseClass = as.character(DiseaseClass)) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Genotype, .keep_all = TRUE)

# for each disease class, mean log2FC per protein across its KO columns
dc_means_list <- lapply(names(disease_classes), function(dc) {
  genotypes_dc <- disease_classes[[dc]]
  cols_dc <- ko_cols_umap[sub("_(iN|iDA)$", "", ko_cols_umap) %in% genotypes_dc]
  if (length(cols_dc) == 0) return(NULL)

  col_name <- gsub("\\.", "_", dc)
  means    <- rowMeans(umap_feat_mat[, cols_dc, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  setNames(data.frame(Genes = rownames(umap_feat_mat), mean = means), c("Genes", col_name))
})
dc_means_list <- Filter(Negate(is.null), dc_means_list)

dc_means_df <- Reduce(function(a, b) dplyr::left_join(a, b, by = "Genes"), dc_means_list)
umap_df     <- umap_df %>% dplyr::left_join(dc_means_df, by = "Genes")

# dc_col_names: underscore versions of disease class names, present in umap_df
dc_col_names <- gsub("\\.", "_", names(disease_classes))
dc_col_names <- dc_col_names[dc_col_names %in% colnames(umap_df)]

# save source file
readr::write_csv(umap_df, file.path(out_dir_d50_UMAP, "UMAP_protein_sourcedata.csv"))


# --- Step 4: Plotting function (categorical color scale)
# aspect.ratio = 1 forces square plotting area; legend at bottom
plot_umap_cat <- function(df, color_col, color_map, title, out_path) {
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = .data[[color_col]])) +
    geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_color_manual(values = color_map, na.value = "grey92", name = NULL) +
    labs(title = title, x = "UMAP1", y = "UMAP2") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 6) +
    theme(panel.grid    = element_blank(),
          axis.text     = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks    = element_blank(),
          aspect.ratio  = 1,
          legend.position = "bottom")

  ggsave(out_path, p, width = 4, height = 4, device = cairo_pdf)
}


# --- Step 5: Combined disease class – categorical
# color map: dc_col_names (underscore versions) → disease_colors (original names)
dc_name_map_ext  <- setNames(names(disease_classes), gsub("\\.", "_", names(disease_classes)))
dc_color_map_ext <- c(
  setNames(disease_colors[dc_name_map_ext[dc_col_names]], dc_col_names),
  None = "grey75"
)

# assign each protein to disease class with max |mean log2FC|; < 0.1 → "None"
disease_class_assign_ext <- umap_df %>%
  dplyr::select(Genes, all_of(dc_col_names)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -Genes, names_to = "DiseaseClass", values_to = "mean_log2fc") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(mean_log2fc)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Genes) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(abs(mean_log2fc), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(TopDiseaseClass = dplyr::if_else(abs(mean_log2fc) < 0.1, "None", DiseaseClass)) %>%
  dplyr::select(Genes, TopDiseaseClass)

umap_df <- umap_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(disease_class_assign_ext, by = "Genes") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(TopDiseaseClass = dplyr::coalesce(TopDiseaseClass, "None"))

plot_umap_cat(
  umap_df, "TopDiseaseClass", dc_color_map_ext,
  "UMAP – Top disease class (max |mean log2FC|, threshold 0.1)",
  file.path(out_dir_d50_UMAP, "UMAP_top_disease_class.pdf")
)

readr::write_csv(
  umap_df %>% dplyr::select(Genes, UMAP1, UMAP2, TopDiseaseClass),
  file.path(out_dir_d50_UMAP, "UMAP_top_disease_class_sourcedata.csv")
)


# --- Step 6: Per-class highlight plots
# one plot per disease class: target class in disease color, all others grey92
for (dc_hl in dc_col_names) {

    dplyr::mutate(highlight = dplyr::if_else(TopDiseaseClass == dc_hl, dc_hl, "Other"))

  plot_umap_cat(

  )

  readr::write_csv(
    umap_df_hl %>% dplyr::select(Genes, UMAP1, UMAP2, highlight),
    file.path(out_dir_d50_UMAP, paste0("UMAP_", dc_hl, "_highlight_sourcedata.csv"))
  )
}

# update master source file with TopDiseaseClass
readr::write_csv(umap_df, file.path(out_dir_d50_UMAP, "UMAP_protein_sourcedata.csv"))
```

# Linear regression on gene level across neurontypes
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------- #
# Linear regression on neuro nDIA dataset
# Plot average correlation per annotation across genotypes
# --------------------------------------------------- #

### ---- Per-Gene Linear Modeling ----
# This script performs gene-specific linear regression to identify differential
# expression based on genotype and neuron type, accounting for experimental day.

# --- 1. Prepare and Factorize Data
# Filter out missing values and convert 'neuron' and 'genotype' to factors.
# 'iN' is set as the reference level for 'neuron'.
lm_results_gx2 <- clean_d50_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(fold_change), !is.na(genotype), !is.na(neuron)) %>%
  mutate(
    neuron   = factor(neuron, levels = c("iN", "iDA")),
    genotype = factor(genotype)
  )


# --- Step 2. Fit Per-Gene Linear Models
# Group data by gene, nest, and fit a linear model for 'fold_change' explained by
# 'genotype', 'neuron', their interaction, and 'day'.
lm_results <- lm_results_gx2 %>%
  group_by(Genes) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(data, ~ tryCatch(
      lm(fold_change ~ genotype * neuron + day, data = .x),
      error = function(e) NULL
    ))),
    tidy = map(model, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) broom::tidy(.x) else tibble() %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  filter(!is.na(p.value))


# --- Step 3. Add Q-values (FDR Corrected P-values)
# Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction to p-values
# within each 'term' category to control for multiple comparisons.
lm_results_df <- lm_results %>%
  group_by(term) %>%
  mutate(q.value = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup()


# --- Step 4: Filter for Significant Terms
# Filter for terms with a q-value (FDR-adjusted p-value) less than 0.05.
sig_genes_df <- lm_results_df %>%
  filter(q.value < 0.05)


# --- Step 5. Filter and Extract Interaction Terms
# Isolate significant **genotype:neuron interaction terms** and extract the
# genotype and neuron types for easier interpretation.
sig_hits <- sig_genes_df %>%
  filter(str_detect(term, "genotype") & str_detect(term, "neuron")) %>%
  mutate(
    genotype = str_extract(term, "(?<=genotype)[^:]+"),
    neuron = str_extract(term, "(?<=:neuron)[^:]+")
  )


# --- Step 6. Identify Top Genes by Absolute Effect Size
# For each genotype, select the top 5 genes with the largest absolute interaction
# effect size (estimate).
top_hits <- sig_hits %>%
  group_by(genotype) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = abs(estimate), n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()


# --- Step 7. Plot Results
# Generate a scatter plot showing interaction effect sizes. Point size indicates
# significance (-log10(q-value)), and `ggrepel` labels the top genes.
d50_LinReg_plot <- ggplot(sig_hits, aes(x = interaction(genotype, neuron), y = estimate)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = -log10(q.value)), alpha = 0.7, color = "#1f78b4") +
  geom_text_repel(data = top_hits, aes(label = Genes),
                  size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 100) +
  labs(title = "Top Differential Effects per Genotype:Neuron Interaction",
       x = "Genotype : Neuron", y = "Effect Size",
       size = "-log10(q-value)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  coord_flip()


# --- Step 8. Save Results
# Save the generated plot and the data frame of all significant terms.
ggsave(file.path(out_dir_d50_LinReg,"diff132_d50_LinReg.pdf"), d50_LinReg_plot, width = 8, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)
write_csv(sig_genes_df, file=file.path(out_dir_d50_LinReg, "diff132_d50_LinReg_significant_genotype_hits.csv"))

```


## Stratified linear modeling of genotype effects by neuron type
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------- #
# Linear regression on neuro nDIA dataset
# Stratified linear modeling of genotype effects by neuron type
# --------------------------------------------------- #

# --- Step 1. Prepare input data
# Filter out incomplete rows and ensure proper factor encoding
lm_input_df <- clean_d50_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(fold_change), !is.na(genotype), !is.na(neuron)) %>%
  mutate(
    genotype = factor(genotype),
    neuron   = factor(neuron)
  )


# --- Step 2. Stratified linear regression function
# This function fits a linear model (fold_change ~ genotype + day)
# for each gene within a specified neuron type (iN or iDA)
fit_stratified_model <- function(df, neuron_label) {
  df %>%
    filter(neuron == neuron_label) %>%
    group_by(Genes) %>%
    nest() %>%
    mutate(
      # Remove NA rows inside nested data
      data = map(data, ~ .x %>% drop_na(fold_change, genotype, day)),

      # Fit model only if gene has sufficient variation
      model = map(data, ~ {
        d <- .x
        if (n_distinct(d$genotype) < 2 || n_distinct(d$day) < 2) return(NULL)
        lm(fold_change ~ genotype + day, data = d)
      }),

      # Extract tidy output if model succeeded
      tidy = map(model, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) broom::tidy(.x) else NULL)
    ) %>%
    filter(!map_lgl(tidy, is.null)) %>%     # keep only successful fits
    dplyr::select(Genes, tidy) %>%
    unnest(tidy) %>%
    mutate(neuron = neuron_label)
}


# --- Step 3. Run model for each neuron type
lm_in_df  <- fit_stratified_model(lm_input_df, "iN")
lm_ida_df <- fit_stratified_model(lm_input_df, "iDA")

# Combine results from both neuron types
lm_neuronwise_df <- bind_rows(lm_in_df, lm_ida_df)


# --- Step 4. Adjust p-values for multiple testing
# Apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction within each term × neuron group
lm_neuronwise_df <- lm_neuronwise_df %>%
  group_by(term, neuron) %>%
  mutate(q.value = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup()


# --- Step 5. Extract and summarize significant results
# Keep only genotype-related terms (omit intercept), FDR < 0.05
ko_terms_sig <- lm_neuronwise_df %>%
  filter(str_detect(term, "^genotype"), term != "(Intercept)", q.value < 0.05)

# For each genotype × neuron term, get top 3 genes by effect size
top_ko_hits <- ko_terms_sig %>%
  group_by(term, neuron) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = abs(estimate), n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()


# --- Step 6. Visualization: Effect sizes for significant genotype terms
d50_LinRegNeuron_plot <- ggplot(ko_terms_sig, aes(x = term, y = estimate, fill = neuron)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.2, size = 0.3) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = top_ko_hits,
    aes(label = Genes),
    size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 100
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("iDA" = "dodgerblue", "iN" = "#F08080")) +
  labs(
    title = "Significant Genotype Effects by Neuron Type",
    x = "Genotype (KO vs ctrl)", y = "Estimated Effect",
    fill = "Neuron"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  coord_flip()


# --- Step 7. Save output
# Save plot as PDF
ggsave(file.path(out_dir_d50_LinReg,"diff132_d50_LinReg_byNeuron.pdf"), d50_LinRegNeuron_plot, width = 8, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)

# Export top hits to CSV
write_csv(top_ko_hits, file=file.path(out_dir_d50_LinReg, "diff132_d50_LinReg_significant_genotype_hits_neuron.csv"))

```


# Limma linear modeling
Use-Case for limma (Linear Models for Microarray/omics Data)

limma is highly optimized for large-scale omics data where:
	•	Genes are modeled in parallel.
	•	The number of observations per gene is small (e.g. 3–5 replicates per condition).
	•	You want borrowing of variance information across genes to stabilize estimates.

Advantages:
	•	Empirical Bayes moderation of standard errors → improves power when sample size is small.
	•	Efficient for batch comparisons, e.g. all KOs vs ctrl.
	•	Handles complex designs via model.matrix().
	•	Very fast for large matrices.

Best suited if:
	•	Your data is already log-transformed intensities or fold changes.
	•	You want to test contrasts like:
	•	KO vs ctrl in iDA
	•	KO vs ctrl in iN
	•	KO effect shared across both neuron types
	•	Interaction (is KO effect different in iDA vs iN)
	
	
	Design Matrix: 
	design <- model.matrix(~ genotype * neuron, data = sample_meta)
	
	This generates three types of terms in your model:
	1.	Main effect of genotype
  	•	Measures how each genotype differs from the reference genotype in the reference neuron type (e.g. iDA).
  	•	Use when you’re asking: “Does genotype X differ from control in iDA neurons?”
	2.	Main effect of neuron
  	•	Measures the effect of switching from iDA to iN in the reference genotype (e.g. control).
  	•	Use when you’re asking: “Is there a baseline difference between neuron types in controls?”
	3.	Interaction: genotype:neuron
  	•	Tests whether the effect of genotype differs between neuron types.
  	•	Use when you’re asking: “Is the genotype effect different in iN vs iDA?”
  	•	This tells you if there’s a non-additive (context-specific) effect of the mutation in iN.

```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------- #
# Linear regression on neuro nDIA dataset
# Limma linear modeling
# --------------------------------------------------- #
# --- 0. create output directory 
out_dir_d50_LinReg_limma <- "/Users/felix/Documents/PostDoc/Harvard/03_LSD-PD/Proteomics/d50_diff132/day50/LinReg/limma_all_coef"
dir.create(out_dir_d50_LinReg_limma, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
out_dir_d50_LinReg_limma_select <- "/Users/felix/Documents/PostDoc/Harvard/03_LSD-PD/Proteomics/d50_diff132/day50/LinReg/limma_select"
dir.create(out_dir_d50_LinReg_limma_select, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Linear model: ~ genotype * neuron
# - Main effect of genotype: difference of KO vs control in reference neuron (here -> iN)
# - Main effect of neuron: difference between iN vs iDA in control genotype
# - Interaction (genotype:neuron): difference in KO effect between iN and iDA
# 
# File explaination 
# - MAplot_iN_genotypeKO ==> effect of  KO vs control in iN (reference neuron)
# - MAplot_iN_genotypeKO.neuroniDA ==> difference in KO effect between iDA and iN. Does the KO behave differently in iDA compared to iN
# - MAplot_iDA_genotype…KOgenotypeKO.neuroniDA ==> effect of  KO vs control in iDA neurons
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

diff132_long_reps <- read.csv('/Users/felix/Documents/PostDoc/Harvard/03_LSD-PD/Proteomics/d50_diff132/day50/datasets/lsd_pro_long.csv', 
                                    header = TRUE, sep = ',', stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


# --- Step 1.Filter out QC samples (NA genotype)
##          Filter out contaminant proteins
contaminant_genes <- c(
  "KRT8", "KRT19", "KRT9", "KRT10", "KRT2", "KRT18", "KRT1", "KRT5",
  "COL10A1", "COL13A1", "COL14A1", "COL18A1", "COL1A1", "COL1A2",
  "COL26A1", "COL2A1", "COL4A1", "COL4A2", "COL5A1", "COL6A1", "COL6A2"
  )

df_day50_filtered <- diff132_long_reps %>%
  filter(!is.na(genotype)) %>%
  filter(!Genes %in% contaminant_genes)



# --- Step 2. Create unique sample IDs from experimental metadata
df_day50_filtered <- df_day50_filtered %>%
  mutate(sample_id = paste(day, genotype, neuron, replicate, sep = "_"))


# --- Step 3. Pivot to wide format using unique sample IDs
expr_df <- df_day50_filtered %>%
  group_by(Genes, sample_id) %>%
  summarise(quan_0 = mean(quan_0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample_id, values_from = quan_0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Genes")


expr_mat <- expr_df %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  as.matrix()

# Log2-transform the expression matrix to stabilize variance
expr_mat <- log2(expr_mat + 1)  # add pseudocount to avoid log(0)



# --- Step 4.  clean df from NA, prepare metadata, and align samples
##          run limma 
# Impute NAs with row means
expr_mat[is.na(expr_mat)] <- rowMeans(expr_mat, na.rm = TRUE)[row(expr_mat)[is.na(expr_mat)]]

# Prepare sample metadata
sample_meta <- df_day50_filtered %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_id, genotype, neuron) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(sample_id = make.names(sample_id))

# Align samples
colnames(expr_mat) <- make.names(colnames(expr_mat))
matching_ids <- intersect(colnames(expr_mat), sample_meta$sample_id)
expr_mat <- expr_mat[, matching_ids]
sample_meta <- filter(sample_meta, sample_id %in% matching_ids)

## check metadata: how many replicates per genotype X celltype?
table(sample_meta$genotype, sample_meta$neuron)

# Set reference level
sample_meta <- sample_meta %>%
  mutate(
    genotype = factor(genotype),
    neuron = factor(neuron, levels = c("iN", "iDA"))  # iN as reference
  )

# Full model with interaction
design <- model.matrix(~ genotype * neuron, data = sample_meta)
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))

# Fit model
fit <- lmFit(expr_mat, design)
fit <- eBayes(fit)

# Construct contrast matrix: iDA KO vs iDA ctrl = genotypeKO + genotypeKO:neuroniDA
contrasts_list <- colnames(design)
ko_levels <- grep("^genotype", contrasts_list, value = TRUE)
interaction_levels <- grep("^genotype.*:neuron", contrasts_list, value = TRUE)

# Extract KO names (excluding 'ctrl')
ko_names <- grep("^genotype(?!ctrl)", colnames(design), value = TRUE, perl = TRUE)

# Build iDA contrasts and store valid entries
ida_contrasts_list <- lapply(ko_names, function(ko) {
  interaction_term <- paste0(ko, ".neuroniDA")
  if (all(c(ko, interaction_term) %in% colnames(design))) {
    return(paste0(ko, " + ", interaction_term))
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
})

# Filter out NULLs
valid_idx <- !sapply(ida_contrasts_list, is.null)
ida_contrasts <- unlist(ida_contrasts_list[valid_idx])
names(ida_contrasts) <- gsub("^genotype", "iDA_", ko_names[valid_idx])

# Create contrast matrix
contrast_matrix <- makeContrasts(contrasts = ida_contrasts, levels = design)

# Fit contrasts
fit_contrasts <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrast_matrix)
fit_contrasts <- eBayes(fit_contrasts)



# --- Step 5. save limma results in output dir & save MA plot for each coefficient 
# Initialize list for saving variables 
results_all <- list()

# Loop through coefficients
# Combine all coefficient names: original + iDA contrasts
# Track coefficients from original and contrast fits
all_coef_names <- c(colnames(fit$coefficients), colnames(fit_contrasts$coefficients))
fit_sources <- c(rep("fit", ncol(fit)), rep("fit_contrasts", ncol(fit_contrasts)))

for (i in seq_along(all_coef_names)) {
  coef_name <- all_coef_names[i]
  fit_obj <- if (fit_sources[i] == "fit") fit else fit_contrasts
  prefix <- if (fit_sources[i] == "fit") "iN_" else "iDA_"

  res <- topTable(fit_obj, coef = coef_name, number = Inf, adjust.method = "BH") %>%
    rownames_to_column("Genes")

  matched_idx <- match(res$Genes, rownames(expr_mat))
  valid_idx <- which(!is.na(matched_idx))
  res <- res[valid_idx, ]
  matched_idx <- matched_idx[valid_idx]

  res <- res %>%
    mutate(
      coef = coef_name,
      baseMean = rowMeans(expr_mat[matched_idx, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
      log2FoldChange = log2(abs(logFC) + 1e-6) * sign(logFC),
      baseMean_log2  = log2(baseMean + 1e-6),
      padj = adj.P.Val,
      sig = case_when(
        #padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange > log2(1.3)  ~ "Up",        # BH-adjusted p-value
        #padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange < -log2(1.3) ~ "Down",      # BH-adjusted p-value
        P.Value < 0.01 & log2FoldChange > log2(2)  ~ "Up",      # raw p-value
        P.Value < 0.01 & log2FoldChange < -log2(2) ~ "Down",    # raw p-value
        TRUE ~ "NS"
      )
    )

  # Save per-contrast CSV
  write.csv(
    res,
    file = file.path(out_dir_d50_LinReg_limma, paste0("limma_results_", prefix, make.names(coef_name), ".csv")),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  # Plot
  top_genes <- res %>% filter(sig != "NS") %>%
    slice_max(order_by = abs(log2FoldChange), n = 50)
  df_ns  <- res %>% filter(sig == "NS")
  df_sig <- res %>% filter(sig != "NS")

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = df_ns, aes(x = baseMean, y = log2FoldChange),
               color = "gray70", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = df_sig, aes(x = baseMean, y = log2FoldChange, color = sig),
               size = 2.0) +
    geom_text_repel(data = top_genes,
                    aes(x = baseMean, y = log2FoldChange, label = Genes, color = sig),
                    size = 3, box.padding = 0.5, point.padding = 1,
                    max.overlaps = 75, segment.color = "grey50") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Down" = "#1465AC", "Up" = "#B31B21")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    labs(
      x = "Mean Abundance",
      y = "Log2 Fold Change",
      title = paste("MA Plot:", prefix, coef_name),
      color = "Significance"
    ) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(out_dir_d50_LinReg_limma, paste0("MAplot_", prefix, make.names(coef_name), ".pdf")),
    plot = p, width = 8, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf
  )

  results_all[[paste0(prefix, coef_name)]] <- res
}

# Combine and save all results
results_all_df <- bind_rows(results_all, .id = "coef")
write.csv(results_all_df, file.path(out_dir_d50_LinReg_limma, "limma_results_all.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# UMAP Parameters Explained

# 	•	Defines the distance metric used in high-dimensional space.
# 	•	Common options:
# 	•	"euclidean": straight-line distance.
# 	•	"manhattan": sum of absolute differences.
# 	•	"cosine": angle-based, good for sparse / high-dimensional data.
# 	•	"correlation": clusters based on expression pattern, not magnitude (useful for gene-level analysis).
```
